newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota seen raising 96/97 annual dividend - paper.
newsitem.headline: Toyota seen raising 96/97 annual dividend - paper.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp is expected to raise its annual dividend for the year to March 31 by one to two yen from 19 yen in 1995/96, a Japanese economic daily said over the weekend.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Sunday that the expected increase in the dividend was due to good earnings pushed up by the weaker yen.
If Toyota actually raises the dividend, it would be the first increase in eight years, the paper said.
Toyota's parent current profit in 1996/97 is expected to rise to 530 billion yen, up 55 percent from the previous year.
Toyota officials were not immediately available for comment.
But industry analysts have told Reuters that Toyota would likely post profits of around 250 billion yen in the six months to September 30, 1996.
Some of the analysts have said the company's 1996/97 full-year parent current profit could reach 550 billion to 600 billion yen amid the current yen/dollar situation.
